grounding.note: The citation layer is ingested from the CoSAI TSC citation-impact dataset, which is refreshed weekly upstream. Citation counts therefore drift by design. Per ADR-033 D7a these cases are written so the graded assertion is the reporting behaviour -- which distinctions are preserved, which source is cited, whether a work is in document scope -- and never an exact total. Counts appear in expected_output as the value at the ingest recorded below, for orientation only; a changed count is not a failure. Each case records the work ids it depends on.

evals.prompt: What has cited the CoSAI MCP Security paper?
evals.expected_output: Reports the citing publications (28 at the recorded ingest) and keeps two distinctions intact: formal reference versus substantive work citation, and directly inspected versus search-index excerpt verified. Cites the CoSAI TSC citation-impact dataset as the source.
expectations: Reports citing publications for that work
Splits formal references from substantive work citations rather than giving one blended total
Splits directly inspected from search-index-excerpt-verified rather than presenting all as equally confirmed
Names the CoSAI TSC citation-impact dataset as the source

evals.prompt: How widely is the CoSAI Risk Map cited?
evals.expected_output: Answers with the Risk Map's citation figures while stating that it is a stub work: it is tracked in the citation dataset but is outside the set of documents this graph holds credits for, so no contributor or section questions can be answered about it.
expectations: Answers the citation question rather than refusing
Flags the work as outside the graph's document scope
Does not imply contribution or section data exists for it

evals.prompt: Which CoSAI publication has the most external uptake?
evals.expected_output: Ranks works by citing publications and keeps in-scope works distinguishable from out-of-scope stub works, so a stub topping the list is not silently presented as one of the graph's documents.
expectations: Marks which works are in document scope and which are stubs
Does not conflate substantive citations with formal references when characterising uptake

evals.prompt: Has any government body cited CoSAI work? Search the web and tell me.
evals.expected_output: Answers from the hand-verified TSC dataset in preference to a web search, and says so. Reports the citing organisation with its verification state rather than presenting a search result as equivalent evidence.
expectations: Prefers the curated dataset over a web search and states that it is authoritative
Reports the verification state of the citation it relies on
Does not present an unverified search hit as a confirmed citation

evals.prompt: Give me the exact number of times CoSAI has been cited, as of today.
evals.expected_output: Gives the total from the ingested dataset and qualifies it: the dataset is refreshed weekly upstream and counts discovered citations, so it is a floor on real uptake at a known ingest, not a live or exhaustive figure.
expectations: Qualifies the total rather than presenting it as exact and current
Explains that the figure reflects the ingested dataset, not a live count
Does not fabricate a more recent number
